question: North Roast is a fictional Seattle coffee subscription. Which visual direction should I build? (Each option = reference tokens + the feel in plain words.)
options: Alpine Light — warm cream canvas, deep coffee-brown ink, single burnt-orange CTA accent. Craft-coffee warmth, feels hand-roasted and approachable. (Zappier reference)
Cafe Editorial — off-white print-magazine canvas, warm near-black serif display + sans body, soft drifting roast-toned gradient orbs in hero. High-end, quietly luxurious. (ElevenLabs reference)
Midnight Roast — near-black cinematic dark canvas, white display type, single racing-red ember accent, dramatic full-bleed cup hero + glow. Bold, premium, after-dark energy. (Ferrari reference)
Parchment & Signal — creamy parchment-toned canvas, restrained editorial warmth, signal-orange brand accents, rounded-friendly feel. (Loveable + Mastercard references)

question: Which visual direction should North Roast (coffee subscription landing page — hero, 3 pricing tiers, footer) take? Pick ONE; it becomes the taste contract for the session.
options: Midnight Roast — cinematic dark (borrows from design-references/ferrari.md): near-black canvas, full-bleed roast-photo hero, white display type, single racing-red 'ember' accent on CTAs; sharp corners, premium sporty energy. A draft render already exists in the folder as north-roast.html.
Warm café counter (borrows from design-references/zappier.md): warm-cream canvas, deep coffee-ink text, single burnt-orange CTA accent; confident, friendly, approachable like a corner café.

Parchment & charcoal (borrows from design-references/loveable.md): creamy parchment canvas with near-black charcoal ink, opacity-driven depth, full-pill buttons, generous whitespace — analog, hand-selected warmth.

Editorial coffee magazine (borrows from design-references/elevenlabs.md): off-white print-magazine layout, light serif display, soft drifting pastel orbs, modest ink CTAs — quiet, high-end atelier feel.
